core.title: Keep each product capability definition semantically coherent
core.given: Any product capability definition (complete or incomplete)
core.when: the planner creates, edits or validates that product capability definition
core.then: Make the product capability semantically coherent: the subject can perform the action, the action serves the goal, the outcome is a measurable result of the action, and the context makes sense for when/where the action occurs.
prefer: Phrase the outcome as a measurable result of the action
Declare as produce only artifacts this product capability owns, and mark at least one produce artifact scope: 'external'
Declare as consume only artifacts owned by other product capabilities
avoid: A subject that cannot perform the action, or an action that does not serve the goal
Outcomes that are not a measurable result of the action
Context that does not make sense for when/where the action occurs
Listing as produce an artifact not owned by this product capability
Consuming an artifact owned by this same product capability
A product capability with no produce artifact of scope: 'external'
core.why: A product capability must be semantically coherent: subject/action/goal align, outcome is measurable, produce is owned, consume is foreign, and at least one produce is external.
evidence: Each coherence check passes on the product capability definition: subject↔action, action↔goal, outcome measurable from action, context makes sense for when/where action occurs
Every produce artifact is owned by this product capability; every consume artifact is owned by a different product capability
At least one produce artifact has scope: 'external'
verification: A semantic-coherence validation runs over each product capability definition and verifies seven properties: (1) the subject can perform the action; (2) the action serves the goal; (3) the outcome is a measurable result of the action; (4) every produce artifact is owned by this product capability; (5) every consume artifact is owned by a different product capability; (6) the context makes sense for when/where the action occurs; (7) at least one produce artifact has scope 'external'.

The ownership and scope properties (4, 5, 7) are mechanically decidable from artifact ownership/scope; the alignment properties (1, 2, 3) and the context property (6) are semantic and are judged rather than mechanically decided.

Activation scope: the capability-definition file kind is the primary and sufficient trigger and the constraint is unconditional — it applies to complete and incomplete product capability definitions alike; field-level change facts and task terms are informational signals only, not gates, and the rule always applies to the whole product capability definition regardless of which field changed.

fires: Planner writes a new product capability definition, even if some fields are still missing
Planner edits any part of an existing product capability definition, including formatting
Planner adds or moves a produce or consume artifact on a product capability
Planner reviews or validates an existing product capability definition
doesNotFire: Editing feature or code files that do not touch any product capability definition
Editing a theme or user/system flow document that contains no product capability definition

neutralityNotes: This convention is inherently method-level: its subject is the product capability definition, an ATDD plan artifact (the vocabulary itself defines 'product capability' as a bounded slice of the product and carries capability/user-system-flow/feature URNs), so terms like product capability, user/system flow, theme, feature and the capability-definition field model (subject, action, goal, outcome, context, produce, consume, scope 'external') are cross-stack plan-artifact concepts and stay in the core rather than in the profile. The rule names no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, path or file suffix; the only profile input needed is which concrete artifact kind plays the capability-definition plan-artifact role. The solely Bun-specific residue is the rule's own term id (coherence_check) and a source-provenance fragment, both carried in bunOnly/dropped without changing the obligation. The Bun-side splitSuggestion (artifact-ownership coherence as a separate rule) is a rewrite-time note, not an agent-facing item, so it is not classified; the core keeps the ownership/external-produce requirements in prefer/avoid/evidence/verification exactly where the Bun rewrite keeps them, so the instantiated obligation is identical.
